verdicts.title: Grad-parity harness is non-deterministic under dropout and mis-attributes the failure to the patches
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end on the current tree with .venv (transformers 5.15.1, torch 2.14.0). get_tiny_config_kwargs() (_test_utils.py:14-27) sets no dropout keys and _base_config_kwargs('gpt2') (test_parity.py:157-168) only pops num_key_value_heads/rope_theta, so GPT2Config keeps resid_pdrop=embd_pdrop=attn_pdrop=0.1 (verified by constructing the tiny config). assert_parity_grad (:450-502) and assert_parity_vmap_grad (:517-563) both put the unpatched reference and the patched model into .train() and run them back to back with no reseed. Running the two helpers directly: dropout 0.1 -> assert_parity_grad FAILS with 'backward grad transformer.h.0.attn.c_attn.bias mismatch: abs_err=1.93e-02, rel_err=5.30e+01' and assert_parity_vmap_grad FAILS with abs_err=1.12e-02; dropout 0.0 -> both PASS, and a direct comparison shows 0 of 16 gradients differ under torch.equal (bit-exact) with identical losses. So the skip reason 'kv_cache/batchify patches alter backward graph' (test_parity.py:97-99) is wrong and gpt2's backward is bit-exact. CORRECTION to the stated mechanism: it is not two different dropout masks off a shared RNG. The patched model has dropout deliberately zeroed by the `dropout` compat patch (_router.py:161-168 -> components/dropout.py disable_dropout), which is on by default whenever compat=True. Measured: the patched model in .train() returns the same loss (4.912911415) on three consecutive draws and in .eval(), while the unpatched reference varies (4.910572052 / 4.887429237 / 4.908598423). The comparison is therefore stochastic-vs-deterministic, not mask-vs-mask; a reseed alone would NOT fix it, only equalizing the dropout rate does. The forward-looking claim checks out: enumerating every registered family's config defaults shows gpt2 is the only one with a nonzero default dropout rate. Already tracked: open issue #813 'Convert parity skips to strict xfail and resolve the gpt2 gradient mismatch' owns this, and its open PR #1032 applies exactly this finding's fix (adds attn_pdrop=embd_pdrop=resid_pdrop=0.0 to _base_config_kwargs for gpt2 and drops gpt2 from the grad exemptions), with a PR body that states the dropout root cause. Severity lowered from medium to low: this is a test-harness artifact with no user-facing behavior change, confined to one family, and already remediated in an open PR.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: On the current tree, assert_parity_grad / assert_parity_vmap_grad on GPT2LMHeadModel with the suite's tiny config (which leaves GPT-2's default resid_pdrop=embd_pdrop=attn_pdrop=0.1) compare a stochastic-dropout unpatched reference against a patched model whose dropout the `dropout` compat patch has zeroed, so all 16 parameter gradients and the loss differ (c_attn.bias abs_err=1.93e-02 backward, 1.12e-02 vmap). Setting the three rates to 0.0 makes the gradients bit-identical (0/16 differ under torch.equal) and both helpers pass, proving gpt2's backward path is exact and the recorded skip reason ('kv_cache/batchify patches alter backward graph') mis-attributes the failure. Impact is test-integrity only: one registered family was written off as having broken gradients when it is bit-exact, and any future family with a nonzero default dropout rate would false-fail the same way (gpt2 is the only such family today).
verdicts._fix_note: The correct fix is to equalize the dropout rate in the reference config (what PR #1032 does), not to reseed the RNG between the two runs as the finding's fix_sketch suggests as an alternative - reseeding does not help, because the patched model has no dropout at all.

verdicts.title: GPT-2 is the documented quick-start model and a listed compatible family, but its per-example gradients diverge from upstream by 53x relative error
verdicts.reasoning: The premise - that patched GPT-2's per-example gradients materially diverge from the model's true gradients - does not hold. The 53x relative error the finding quotes is the same number I reproduce, but it is an artifact of the parity harness, not of the patched model. The harness compares an unpatched reference running GPT-2's default stochastic training dropout (resid_pdrop=embd_pdrop=attn_pdrop=0.1, which the tiny config never zeroes) against a patched model whose dropout the `dropout` compat patch has zeroed by design (_router.py:161-168 -> components/dropout.py disable_dropout, on by default under compat=True; the module docstring gives the rationale: DP-SGD trains without dropout and SDPA's fused dropout is vmap-incompatible). Measured: the patched model in .train() returns an identical loss on repeated draws and equal to its .eval() loss (4.912911415 x3), while the unpatched reference varies per draw. Once the reference is given the same dropout-free contract (attn_pdrop=embd_pdrop=resid_pdrop=0.0), assert_parity_grad and assert_parity_vmap_grad both PASS and a direct comparison shows 0 of 16 gradients differ under torch.equal - bit-exact, not merely within tolerance. So a user following the HF quick start on gpt2 does not get materially wrong per-example gradients; they get exactly upstream's gradients for a dropout-free model, which is the intended DP training contract for every family, not something specific to gpt2. The library maintainers reached the same conclusion independently: open PR #1032 (closing #813) states 'The GPT-2 mismatch came from comparing its default stochastic training dropout against Opaque's deterministic DP model preparation ... restoring backward and clipped vmap(grad) parity without changing GPT-2 model behavior or support', and fixes the harness rather than the model. The only residue of this finding is (a) the docs-vs-skipped-test optics, which open issue #813 already owns, and (b) a minor docs gap: docs/user-guide/huggingface/model-patches.md:58 enumerates the compat bucket as eager_attention/batchify/vmap_masking/empty_batches/vmap_checkpointing and never mentions that compat=True also zeroes all model dropout (only docs/alignment/trainers.md:202 and docs/reference/transformers.md:570 document a disable_dropout flag, for the alignment trainers). Neither supports a high-severity 'silently wrong training' claim, and the fix_sketch's recommendation to de-register gpt2 or swap the quick-start model would be acting on a false diagnosis.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: No reproducible defect. Patched GPT-2's backward and clipped vmap(grad) gradients are bit-identical to upstream once both sides use the same dropout rate (0/16 parameters differ under torch.equal); the quoted abs_err=1.93e-02 / rel_err=5.30e+01 comes from the harness comparing a dropout-0.1 reference against a patched model whose dropout the default `dropout` compat patch intentionally zeroes. The residual, much smaller issue is documentation: model-patches.md:58 does not list dropout-zeroing among the compat-bucket effects, so a reader cannot tell that apply_model_patches(compat=True) removes dropout from their model. The docs-promote-gpt2-while-its-parity-tests-are-skipped optics are already tracked by open #813, whose open PR #1032 removes the gpt2 grad exemptions entirely.
verdicts._note: already_tracked set to 813 because the only surviving (test-integrity) portion of this finding is that issue's subject; the finding's own headline claim is refuted.

verdicts.title: Three registered families have no forward-parity coverage either, a hole no child of #769 covers
verdicts.reasoning: Every link verified on the current tree. test_parity.py:86-92 defines _STRICT_FORWARD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES = {'deepseek_v4','gpt_oss','qwen3_next'} and :251-252 skips test_forward_logits_parity for them; :97-103 puts the same three (plus gpt2) in _GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES, applied at :278-279 (test_backward_grads_parity) and :483-484 (test_vmap_grad_parity). So those three families are skipped in all three core parity tests. I checked for coverage elsewhere: grepping the whole opaque-patches test tree shows assert_parity_forward / assert_parity_grad / assert_parity_vmap_grad are used in test_parity.py only, and the dedicated modules test_gpt_oss.py, test_deepseek_v4.py, test_qwen3_next.py contain only smoke tests (forward_no_grad, forward_backward, vmap_grad 'some gradient exists', experts-not-patched) with no upstream comparison. The coverage guard at :509-520 is confirmed blind: it recomputes exactly the expression that defines FAMILIES (supported_families() - _PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES, filtered by find_spec) and asserts families - set(FAMILIES) is empty, so it can never see either skip set (it could only fire if a family were registered after module import, which is not what it advertises). Not a duplicate of the open tracking issue: #813's scope and acceptance criteria are the gradient/vmap-grad exemptions, and its open PR #1032 converts only those to strict xfail while leaving _STRICT_FORWARD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES a plain skip and leaving the coverage guard untouched - so the forward-parity hole and the tautological guard survive #813's resolution. Parent umbrella #769 is open but has no child covering this. Severity kept at medium: no user-visible defect today and no epsilon impact, but three registered supported families have zero upstream-fidelity coverage while a test named test_parity_families_covered actively reports them as covered.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: deepseek_v4, gpt_oss and qwen3_next are registered supported families that are skipped by all three parity tests in packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/test_parity.py (forward at :251-252 via _STRICT_FORWARD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES, backward at :278-279 and vmap-grad at :483-484 via _GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES), and no other test in the package makes any patched-vs-upstream comparison for them - their dedicated modules only assert that a forward runs and that some gradient exists. A patch regression that silently changes their forward logits (a rebound attention forward, a dropped softcap, a mis-scaled RoPE) would produce no test signal, and test_parity_families_covered (:509-520) cannot detect the hole because it re-derives the same set FAMILIES is built from and subtracts only the one-element _PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES. Open PR #1032, which closes the related issue #813, leaves both the forward skip set and this guard unchanged.
verdicts._caveat: The skip reason is partly legitimate for these three: the unpatched reference itself needs runtime shims (gpt_oss and deepseek_v4 are eager-only with attention sinks; qwen3_next's masking uses data-dependent scalar extraction), so a strictly unpatched forward reference may not exist. The actionable defect is the silent exemption plus the guard that misreports coverage, not necessarily the absence of a strict comparison.

verdicts.title: tree_leaves silently returns [] for Opaque wrapper types, the last survivor of the OPQ-333 wrapper-blindness class in the same public facade
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced directly against the installed packages. packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/pytree.py:111-128 is `flat, _ = _ot.tree_flatten(tree); return [x for x in flat if isinstance(x, torch.Tensor)]`; the wrapper types are unregistered frozen dataclasses so they flatten to one non-tensor leaf and are filtered out. Executed: tree_leaves(ClippedPytree(pytree={'g': tensor([3.,4.])}, max_norm=1.0)) -> [] with no warning, while tree_flatten on the same object returns ([ClippedPytree(...)], PyTreeSpec(*)) and global_norm on it raises InputTypeError 'ClippedPytree global norm is unsupported ... Use `.pytree` for an explicit numerical-only view' (pytree.py:377-400). Both names are exported from the same public facade (opaque/pytree.py). The inconsistency is real: the sibling that was hardened by the OPQ-333 fix now rejects these types loudly while its neighbour returns an empty list quietly. Not tracked: issue #807 (OPQ-333, severity low) is closed and its scope was explicitly unscale_grads and global_norm only; PR #869 did not touch tree_leaves. I checked whether the library itself ever feeds a wrapper into tree_leaves - the internal callers (clipping/_pytree.py:475,611, clipping/_distributed.py:141,148,217, distributed/_state.py:331, pytree.py:414) all operate on raw gradient pytrees, so there is no internal miscomputation, which keeps this a user-facing API-consistency defect rather than a numerical one. Severity stays low: no privacy or numerical impact on any library path, and the docstring does say non-tensor leaves are ignored, so the behavior is a fail-open API inconsistency rather than a contract violation.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user holding the ClippedPytree returned by clipped_grad (or the NoisedPytree returned by a noise_fn) calls the public opaque.pytree.tree_leaves on it and gets [] with no error or warning, so hand-rolled diagnostics such as sum(p.square().sum() for p in tree_leaves(grads)) silently read 0.0, or torch.stack(tree_leaves(grads)) raises an empty-list error far from the real cause. The same facade's global_norm raises InputTypeError pointing at .pytree for exactly these four wrapper types, so the two neighbours disagree. No library-internal path is affected (all internal tree_leaves callers receive raw tensor pytrees), so there is no numerical or privacy consequence - observability and API consistency only. Closed issue #807 fixed this class for unscale_grads and global_norm but was scoped not to include tree_leaves.
verdicts._extra: tree_flatten / tree_structure / tree_map share the blindness in different ways: tree_flatten returns the wrapper as a single leaf, and tree_map applies fn to the wrapper object itself (tree_map(lambda x: x*2, clipped) returns ClippedPytree with both the tensors and max_norm doubled, because ClippedPytree defines the arithmetic). Any fix should cover the family, as the finding's fix_sketch suggests.
